text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Rubbish plan authors agree not to disagree. Government announces "temporary" solution to garbage crisis in southern suburbs by opening new dump in area.
- Television workers lament closure of unlicensed stations.
- Brazilian speaker Michel Tamer learns about his roots during tour of "second home".
- Opposition MPs say government is encouraging revolt.
- Government starts work on social sector conference.
- U.S. travel ban decision expected in next few days.
- Lebanon complains to ceasefire committee about warplane attacks.
- Security situation deteriorates in south Lebanon.
- Latest t-bill issue registers deficit of subscription against maturity for first time in a very long time.
- Lebanon and Israel file five complaints to five-nation monitoring committee, formed under terms of April 1996 understanding that ended 17 days of an Israeli blitz on Lebanon.
